# EXCALIBUR Control Center v0.5.1

A native Linux **read-only hardware telemetry control center** for CASPER EXCALIBUR
G870 laptops, delivered as a single Arch Linux package (`excalibur-control-center`)
that contains the Qt6 GUI **and** the `excalibur-wmi` read-only hwmon driver
(integrated DKMS).

This is the **first public release**. The product only reports telemetry — it does
not control any hardware.

## Included

- native Linux hardware telemetry dashboard
- CPU / GPU temperature telemetry
- CPU / GPU fan RPM telemetry
- 60-second telemetry history
- Cooling telemetry / history view
- Device information
- Diagnostics viewer
- JSON diagnostics export
- Theme settings (System / Light / Dark)
- Celsius / Fahrenheit
- configurable refresh interval (1 / 2 / 5 / 10 s)
- system tray + background runtime
- single-instance runtime
- Arch Linux packaging
- integrated DKMS driver

## Not supported

This release does **not** control hardware. There is no fan control, no RGB control,
no power control, no performance mode, and no EC/WMI writes.

## Known limitations

- **Kernel API compatibility:** the driver is verified against the **7.2.x** kernel
  API. It does **not** build against **6.18.x-lts** because
  `wmidev_set_block` / `wmidev_query_block` are absent there. Driver compatibility
  depends on the kernel API.
- **Telemetry fidelity:** the GUI shows raw hwmon values without smoothing or
  filtering; anomalous firmware/EC samples are not hidden.
- **Secure Boot:** the package does not sign kernel modules; on Secure Boot systems
  the user must handle module signing.
- **AUR:** publication is pending registration availability.

## Install (Arch Linux / CachyOS)

The AUR package is not published yet. Until it is available:

- build the package from source (see the repository README), or
- install the release package artifact directly:

  ```bash
  sudo pacman -U excalibur-control-center-0.5.1-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
  ```

The GUI runs without root (unprivileged runtime). Package installation and the DKMS
kernel-module lifecycle may require root.
